human.controls: Arrows move, X acts. Notsnake by Terry Cavanagh: level = seed % 1 of the 1 playable levels; the episode ends when the level is solved.

reference.name: PuzzleScript (increpare): the engine itself, vendored
reference.license: MIT (engine). Games: src/demo/README says only the editor-dropdown examples can be assumed MIT; the corpus is exactly that list.
reference.driving_protocol: compile(["loadLevel", n], text, String(seed)); while (againing) { againing = false; processInput(-1); }; per action a in 0..4: processInput(a) then the same loop; NOOP (5): nothing. unitTesting = false so DoWin sets `winning` instead of calling nextLevel(). The episode ends at winning.
reference.rng: rng.js RC4 keyed by the seed string (RandomGen = new RNG(seed) in loadLevelFromLevelDat); a falsy seed would fall back to Math.random() + Date.now(), so the seed is always a non-empty string
reference.parity: lockstep: convertLevelToString(), sha1(level.objects), curlevel, winning, againing, textMode, messagetext, backups.length, movements all zero, RandomGen RC4 i/j/sha1(s) after reset and after every step (tests/gate_oracle.mjs vs tests/oracle.mjs on the unmodified checkout)
not_matched: pixels: the reference draws at a window-dependent cell size with the canvas letterboxed; PlayTrain draws 5 px cells into a canvas sized for the largest playable level (or the flick/zoom screen) and the rasterizer scales that to 64x64. Sprite ids and positions are gated (G8), pixel values are not
undo (Z), restart (R), level select, the title screen, message screens and the key press that moves from `winning` to the next level: the episode ends at winning (gameState WIN, reward 1)
sound: sfxr is loaded because the compiler needs it; nothing is played
realtime_interval games: none in the corpus; no step model is defined for them
key repeat and the browser's input buffering: one action per step, no repeats
the reset consumes one NOOP frame before the first agent action (PlayTrain draws and steps in the same frame)
light-theme detection: the engine reads document.body.classList for its default colours; the shim reports no light theme (dark defaults), as the reference's own test runner does
